title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, agent-node behaviour, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Both API calls match Microsoft documentation, including the allocation properties; targeted searches found no documented node-specific tenant switch or automation for the human-assistance setting.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The feature uses a consumption-based licensing model measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Variable cost reflects metered Copilot Credit usage.

claims.claim: The tenant-pool control is at Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**. Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**. Select **Manage Copilot Credits**. Select the environment. Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate. Under **Capacity overages**, clear **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and allocation example
claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation and tenant-pool enforcement rule.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: MCSMessages is the entitlement ID used for Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID `MCSMessages` and are managed through the `licensing/allocationsV2` operations of the Power Platform API.

claims.claim: allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity sets the environment's credit allocation.
The allocated entitlement's enforcementRules entry with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false disables tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote:
enforcementRules = @(
                # Disable TenantPool so the environment is capped at its allocation.
                # Set enabled = $true to let the environment draw from tenant capacity.
                @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: The maker reaches human assistance through Workflows > workflow > Build > Add panel > Agent > Request human assistance when unsure.
claims.quote: Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab. Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel. The configuration panel opens for the agent node. ... claims.claim: No API for the node's Request human assistance when unsure setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "human assistance" "API"; "agent node" "table" "entity reference". Opened agent-node-workflow and Agent (bot) table reference; searched the latter for human, assistance, escalation, agent node and workflow; no setting operation found.

claims.claim: No central enforcement setting for Request human assistance when unsure is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Request human assistance when unsure" "enforce"; Copilot Studio workflow agent node human assistance API central enforcement Dataverse table. Read node configuration, data policies and ACP; no central enforcement of this toggle found.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An agent node delegates a workflow step to an AI agent for reasoning.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The agent can call tools during the delegated step.
claims.quote: Equip the agent with tools (Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and connectors) so it can take action.

claims.claim: The agent can read knowledge sources before returning a result.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The response becomes dynamic content for later workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: An existing agent is selected from a list of published agents.
claims.quote: **An existing agent**: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: The existing agent retains its configured instructions, tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow defines an inline agent whose instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape are configured in the node and travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: **New agent for this workflow**: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow. The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: Inline agents cannot be reused outside their workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.claim: Attaching tools to an inline agent is optional.
claims.quote: Give the node an instruction, optionally attach tools and knowledge, and you're done.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No credit rate specific to the agent node is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent node workflow Copilot Credits rate pricing; "agent node" "rate" "Microsoft Copilot harness". Read node page, usage-based billing overview and harness cost table; standard-harness rate search results state their different scope; no node rate found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the work runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: Environment consumption can use prepaid capacity or an environment-linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: Charges are not assigned to individual makers.
claims.quote: and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant prevents spending unallocated tenant prepaid capacity after the allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation.

claims.claim: Turning off tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Azure budgets send notifications but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, rather than only workflows with agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role permitted to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The agent-node Learn page names no licence among its prerequisites for adding a node.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent node workflow Copilot Credits rate pricing. Read the entire agent-node-workflow page, including Add an agent node and billing note; it gives no licence prerequisite for adding the node.

claims.claim: The Workflows page's Credit usage (last 30 days) column reports workflow consumption for that period.
claims.quote: The **Credit usage (last 30 days)** column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.

claims.claim: Eligible environments with no allocation configuration have tenant-pool draw selected by default.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule makes the environment's tenant-draw setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic allocation requests cannot override the group-governed tenant-pool setting.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: The allocation request requires authenticated authorization.
claims.quote:
$auth = Get-MsalToken -ClientId $clientId -TenantId $tenantId -Scope "https://api.powerplatform.com/.default" -Interactive
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The documented allocation example sends Content-Type application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: The example body's scope.environmentId identifies the environment receiving the allocation.
Microsoft documents individual agent monthly limits through Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**. Select **Manage Agents**. Select the agent, and then select **Set limit**. Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.claim: Learn does not state that individual agent monthly limits cap agent-node credit consumption inside a workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio workflow agent node monthly agent limits consumption cap. Read node page, harness cost controls and Manage Copilot Credits capacity page; agent limits and separately billed flows are documented, but no node-within-workflow cap is stated.
